text: The correspondence theory of truth (Russell, Austin) holds that a proposition is true if and only if:
choices: it coheres with a comprehensive, maximally consistent system of beliefs.
believing it 'works'—it is useful and leads to successful action.
it corresponds to a fact or state of affairs that obtains in the world.
asserting it is warranted by our evidence and is verifiable in principle.
explanation: Correspondence theory makes truth a relation between a truth-bearer and a worldly fact or state of affairs (Aristotle's 'to say of what is that it is'). Distractor 0 is the coherence theory and distractor 1 is the pragmatist theory—rival answers to the very same question that locate truth in internal consistency or practical utility rather than word-world correspondence.
